name: Anna Cuomo
title: Anna Cuomo, PhD
eyebrow: Cellular genomics · Human genetics · Drug discovery
bio: I'm an Associate Principal Scientist at AstraZeneca's Centre for Genomic Research based in London. A mathematical engineer turned computational biologist, I work at the meeting point of single-cell genomics and population genetics: I both develop methods to map genetic effects on gene expression in single cells, such as CellRegMap and SAIGE-QTL, and apply them to population-scale cohorts such as TenK10K and HipSci. More recently I use genome-wide perturbation screens to study the precise mechanisms by which genes act in specific cellular types and states. My goal is to understand how natural genetic variation and experimental perturbations shape cells, to reveal mechanism and help find new drug targets.
bioPrevious: Previously an EMBO postdoctoral fellow at the Garvan Institute in Sydney and a postdoc at the Wellcome Sanger Institute; PhD in Statistical Genetics from the University of Cambridge and EMBL-EBI.
description: Associate Principal Scientist at AstraZeneca's Centre for Genomic Research. Cellular genomics, human genetics and drug discovery.
